newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Motorbike maker KTM to go public in Vienna.
newsitem.headline: Motorbike maker KTM to go public in Vienna.

text.p: Austria's lone motorcycle manufacturer KTM Motorradholding AG launched an initial public offering for up to 920,000 shares priced at 500-600 schillings each on Friday.

KTM, which narrowly avoided being run off the road by financial troubles in 1991, will offer 800,000 shares and retain a greenshoe option on another 120,000, co-lead manager Creditanstalt Investment Bank AG said.

The subscription period will run from November 22 to December 5, with the final issue price announced one day before the close. The shares will begin trading on the Vienna stock exchange on December 12.
KTM chief executive Rudolf Knuenz, who played a pivotal role in the firm's 1991 rescue, said proceeds from the sale would go towards financing expansion and developing new products.

He forecast sales and earnings would rise more than 10 percent in the financial year to August 31, 1997. In 1995/6, sales broke through one billion schillings for the first time, bringing a net profit of 26.1 million schillings.
Knuenz said the firm, which specialises in off-road bikes, aimed to sell 17,000 to 18,000 bikes this year, up from 15,000 in 1995/6. -- Vienna Newsroom, 43-1-53112-25
